comment: On the running app. One pixel of drag on Size worth about three per cent of it, no field to type, and '30.34 px' drawing a ring 57 across. The row now reads Radius with a tooltip saying so and that a double-click types one, Left and Right step it a pixel over the slider and ten with Shift, and a drag with Shift held moves a tenth as far. The bar's slider is 179 units wide at 1920 at (1076, 5), so its centre is (1165, 17).
The row and its tooltip, hovered on the bar. 0.023148 of a 1080-tall document is 25 px.
Three presses of Right over the bar's slider are three pixels, 25 to 28. Shift and Right are ten more, 38, and one Left is 37.
With the pointer on the canvas an arrow is not the slider's, and the row stays at 37.

A drag with Shift held. The press carries Shift, so the value does not jump to the pointer, and 18 units right with Shift held are a tenth of a tenth of the box's travel, where the same 18 units without Shift, after Shift is let go, are a tenth of it, ten times the change in the log of the radius on this geometric row.
The typed number the tooltip names, through the row's own field, and then the ring on the canvas: its radius in the ring dump against the number on the bar.
Every FactorSlider has the step, and the keyboard follows the pointer into a docker: Left over the Tool Options docker's Opacity is one per cent less.
